articles.title: Duas mulheres ficam feridas em acidente na Wilson Mendes, em Cabo Frio | G1
articles.standfirst: Batida ocorreu na noite desta quarta-feira (25), em trecho sem iluminação da via. Vítimas foram socorridas pelo Corpo de Bombeiros e levadas para o Hospital Central de Emergências.
articles.summary: Batida ocorreu na noite desta quarta-feira (25), em trecho sem iluminação da via. Vítimas foram socorridas pelo Corpo de Bombeiros e levadas para o Hospital Central de Emergências.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Duas mulheres ficaram feridas em um acidente envolvendo um carro e uma moto na Avenida Wilson Mendes, em Porto do Carro, na altura da entrada para o bairro Jardim Esperança, em Cabo Frio , na Região dos Lagos do Rio. A batida aconteceu por volta das 19h30 desta quarta-feira (25).

Ao g1 , a motorista do carro, que preferiu não se identificar, disse que tentava acessar a Avenida Wilson Mendes por uma saída próxima ao posto de combustíveis quando teve a visão da pista parcialmente bloqueada por outro carro.

Segundo o relato, o automóvel, em vez de esperar atrás do carro dela, parou na lateral, um pouco à frente e sobre os tachões de sinalização, o que prejudicou a visualização do fluxo de veículos no sentido São Pedro da Aldeia.

Ainda conforme a motorista, ao avançar lentamente para entrar na avenida, ela se deparou com a motocicleta e não conseguiu evitar a colisão.

Duas mulheres que estava na moto ficaram feridas e foram levadas para o hospital pelos bombeiros, em Cabo Frio — Foto: Ariane Ludmila Marques/g1

As duas mulheres que estavam na moto, de aproximadamente 30 anos, foram socorridas pelos bombeiros, uma com o quadro moderado e outra em situação mais grave, devido a uma fratura interna.

A condutora do carro afirmou também que o veículo que teria prejudicado sua visibilidade deixou o local logo após o acidente.

Um bombeiro e um médico passavam pelo local no momento do acidente, pararam para dar assistência às vítimas e ajudaram a reforçar o pedido de socorro.

Equipes do Corpo de Bombeiros chegaram em seguida e encaminharam as duas vítimas para o Hospital Central de Emergências (HCE) de Cabo Frio.

Acidente na Av. Wilson Mendes, em Cabo Frio, deixou duas mulheres feridas — Foto: Ariane Marques/g1

A mãe da motorista, que trafegava em outro carro à frente da filha, contou que havia ligado o pisca-alerta do veículo ao perceber a baixa iluminação no trecho da avenida. Pouco depois, ao notar que a filha não seguia atrás, recebeu uma ligação da própria jovem informando sobre o acidente.

Motorista disse que tentava sair para a Avenida Wilson Mendes, em Cabo Frio, quando um carro parou ao lado, um pouco mais à frente, atrapalhando a visibilidade de quem vinha no sentido contrário. Trecho também está sem iluminação — Foto: Ariane Ludmila Marques/g1

Motoristas que passavam pelo local aproveitaram para reclamar das condições de iluminação da via. O acidente ocorreu justamente em um trecho sem luz, em pelo menos, três postes. Um dos postes fica bem em frente à saída onde ocorreu o acidente. Os outros dois estão no outro lado da pista, praticamente na mesma direção.

Outro problema apontado por condutores é a falta de sinalização refletiva na pista, como tachões e dispositivos conhecidos popularmente como "olho de gato", que auxiliam na visibilidade durante a noite.

Até por volta das 20h40, os veículos envolvidos permaneciam no local sob acompanhamento de agentes da Polícia Militar.

O g1 solicitou informações à Prefeitura de Cabo Frio a respeito do problema na iluminação e sinalização viária. A reportagem também perguntou sobre o estado de saúde das vítimas no acidente e aguarda retorno.

articles.title: Mulher arrastada por enxurrada em Goiânia é salva antes de cair em córrego | G1
articles.standfirst: Vítima segurou em um bloco de concreto na margem do córrego até ser retirada por dois homens no Parque Amazônia. Ela foi encaminhada ao Hospital de Urgências de Goiás (Hugo).
articles.summary: Após ser levada pela força da água no Parque Amazônia, a vítima foi socorrida por pedestres e encaminhada ao hospital durante o forte temporal em Goiânia nesta quarta.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Uma mulher foi arrastada pela enxurrada e resgatada antes de cair em um córrego durante um temporal em Goiânia , nesta quarta-feira (25). Vídeo mostra a vítima segurando em um bloco de concreto e sendo retirada do local por dois homens. O zelador de uma escola próxima conversou com a TV Anhanguera e deu mais detalhes sobre o caso, que aconteceu na Avenida Dona Terezinha de Moraes, no Parque Amazônia.

Nas imagens, é possível ver quando a mulher segura em um dos blocos que fica na margem, antes do leito do córrego. Segundo Cilciney Martins dos Santos, zelador de uma escola da região, a mulher gritou bastante pedindo socorro.

"Ela ficou engarranchada (presa) ali, um homem passou com outro, resgatou ela, puxou ela para cá até o Corpo de Bombeiros chegar para levar ela. Ela enganchou lá no concreto e ficou segurando", disse o zelador à TV Anhanguera.

Ainda no vídeo, dois homens aparecem ajudando a mulher a sair do local. Um deles consegue segurá-la e levantá-la, levando-a para perto da calçada, onde outro homem a ajuda a subir e ficar em segurança. Cilciney disse também que o Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) foi até o local para prestar socorro.

O zelador contou que o Corpo de Bombeiros chegou a posicionar uma viatura para pegá-la na parte de baixo, no córrego, mas, como ela já havia sido puxada pelos homens, não foi preciso usar a estrutura dos socorristas. Depois de socorrida, ela foi levada para o Hospital de Urgências de Goiás (Hugo).

O nome da mulher não foi divulgado pelas equipes de resgate e, por isso, até a última atualização desta reportagem, o g1 não conseguiu verificar o estado de saúde dela.

articles.title: Maternidade do Promorar: acordo com MP encerra partos em Teresina | G1
articles.standfirst: Os partos e atendimentos neonatais da Maternidade do Promorar serão transferidos para as unidades Buenos Aires, Wall Ferraz e Satélite. O pré-natal continuará na unidade.
articles.summary: Maternidade do Promorar terá partos transferidos para três hospitais de Teresina após acordo com o MP, mantendo apenas o pré-natal e ganhando novos leitos clínicos.
articles.body:
Acordo entre prefeitura e MP confirma fim dos partos na Maternidade do Promorar, em Teresina — Foto: Reprodução

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Leitos clínicos, obstétricos, neonatais, de saúde mental e de isolamento passarão por mudanças nos hospitais da rede municipal de Teresina. A transferência dos atendimentos de partos, internações de mães e bebês e as urgências obstétricas e neonatais da Maternidade do Promorar para outras unidades da capital está mantida .

As mudanças estão previstas em um Termo de Ajustamento de Conduta (TAC) firmado nesta quarta-feira (25) entre a Prefeitura de Teresina, por meio da Fundação Municipal de Saúde (FMS), e o Ministério Público do Piauí

O acordo prevê a ampliação de leitos clínicos, obstétricos, neonatais, de saúde mental e de isolamento na rede municipal. O documento foi assinado pela presidente da FMS, Leopoldina Cipriano, e pelo promotor de Justiça Marcelo de Jesus Monteiro Araújo, titular da 29ª Promotoria de Justiça de Teresina.

Os atendimentos realizados atualmente na Maternidade do Promorar serão transferidos para as maternidades Buenos Aires, Wall Ferraz e Satélite. Os serviços de pré-natal e acompanhamento puerperal continuarão sendo oferecidos na unidade .

A Maternidade do Promorar também passará por reforma. Após as obras, o local terá 45 leitos clínicos, 10 de saúde mental e seis de isolamento.

Com a implantação dos seis leitos de isolamento no Promorar, Teresina passará a ter 17 leitos desse tipo na rede municipal.

A reforma da unidade tem previsão de começar ainda este ano. Já o Hospital da Primavera terá a capacidade ampliada de 18 para 26 leitos clínicos.

Os leitos de saúde mental que funcionam atualmente na unidade serão transferidos para o Promorar, que passará a contar com uma estrutura específica para esse tipo de atendimento.

CRM cobra explicações da FMS e vistoria Maternidade do Promorar

O Conselho Regional de Medicina do Piauí (CRM-PI) cobrou explicações da FMS e vistoriou, no dia dezoito de novembro, a Maternidade do Promorar, na Zona Sul de Teresina. A fiscalização ocorreu após a prefeitura anunciar a transferência dos leitos obstétricos da unidade a partir de dezembro.

Em reunião realizada no dia 16 de novembro, com representantes da FMS, o CRM-PI decidiu adotar medidas administrativas para acompanhar a mudança.

O conselho enviou um ofício à fundação pedindo informações sobre a distribuição de médicos e pacientes, além da capacidade estrutural e operacional da rede para receber a demanda transferida.

No dia 18 de novembro, o vice-presidente do CRM-PI, Raimundo Sá, vistoriou a estrutura da Maternidade do Promorar. Segundo o conselho, também foram feitas análises nas demais maternidades municipais para avaliar se elas têm capacidade de absorver a demanda.

Procurada, a diretora-geral do Complexo do Promorar, Socorro Oliveira, informou que ainda não havia analisado o ofício enviado pelo CRM-PI.

Maternidade do Promorar: CRM cobra FMS sobre transferência de leitos — Foto: Antonio Fernandes (Rede Clube)

O anúncio da transferência dos partos provocou protestos de profissionais de saúde em frente à maternidade. Moradores da Zona Sul também demonstraram preocupação com possíveis impactos no atendimento às gestantes da região.

A presidente da União Comunitária de Conselhos e Associações (Unicost), Josiane, criticou a falta de diálogo com a comunidade e defendeu a permanência do serviço na unidade:

"Nós estamos aqui hoje por todas as mulheres, por todas as adolescentes, por todas nós da comunidade, todas as mulheres que hoje necessitam dessa maternidade. Essa maternidade aqui é muito importante para a Zona Sul. Nós não podemos perder uma maternidade que é referência há mais de 30 anos, porque o prefeito tá dizendo que existe três partos, que hoje só aqui dentro tem 17", afirmou.

A moradora Vanda afirmou que percebeu melhorias no atendimento da unidade, mas demonstrou preocupação com a distância das maternidades que passarão a receber as gestantes.

A estrutura da maternidade também apresenta problemas, como mofo em paredes, banheiros interditados e camas que precisam de manutenção.

Pela legislação de saúde, gestantes que chegarem à unidade em trabalho de parto deverão ser encaminhadas e transportadas pelo município até a maternidade de referência, com garantia de deslocamento seguro.

articles.title: Tiroteio no Lins: menino de 6 anos e grávida estão entre baleados | G1
articles.standfirst: Menino de 6 anos foi atingido no abdômen e está no centro cirúrgico. Mulher grávida, idosa e barbeiro também foram feridos e levados ao Hospital Salgado Filho
articles.summary: O tiroteio no Lins durante operação policial deixou quatro moradores feridos, incluindo uma criança em estado grave, uma grávida e uma idosa na Zona Norte do Rio.
articles.body:
Um suspeito foi morto e quatro moradores foram baleados durante uma operação da Polícia Civil no Complexo do Lins, na Zona Norte do Rio, na tarde desta quarta-feira (25). Os feridos são um menino de 6 anos, uma mulher grávida, uma idosa e um homem que trabalha como barbeiro.

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Caio Miguel Duarte Pacheco, de 6 anos, foi atingido por um tiro no abdômen e está no centro cirúrgico. Marisa Pinheiro, de 70 anos, foi atingida por estilhaços no pé direito. O barbeiro, identificado como Marcelo, de 25 anos, foi atingido no peito e no pescoço. Os três foram socorridos e levados ao Hospital Salgado Filho.

O Hospital Materno Infantil de Brasília (Hmib), na Asa Sul, está sem oxigênio desde terça-feira (24), segundo servidores e pacientes do local. Os leitos afetados estão sendo abastecidos por cilindros .

Servidores contaram que o problema afetou os atendimentos, a UTI neonatal e impediu internações. O estoque de cilindros teria acabado ainda na tarde de terça.

"Hoje a tarde, a gente teve paciente convulsionando grave, precisando de oxigênio, e ficou na mala [mochila com cilindro] do Samu", contou uma servidora.

A Secretaria de Saúde informou que o problema aconteceu durante uma manutenção no hospital, que causou um rompimento na tubulação de distribuição de oxigênio medicinal. A pasta disse ainda que o problema seria resolvido ainda na terça-feira, mas a TV Globo registrou, na manhã desta quarta (25), que a unidade segue sem oxigênio.

🔎 O Hmib é um hospital público do DF, especializado no atendimento de gestantes, mães, recém-nascidos e crianças.

Hmib interrompe internações após falta de oxigênio — Foto: TV Globo

"A Secretaria de Saúde do Distrito Federal (SES-DF) informa que nenhum paciente ficou sem oxigênio e os procedimentos cirúrgicos ocorreram normalmente.

Durante uma manutenção predial em uma unidade do Hospital Materno Infantil de Brasília (Hmib), houve um rompimento na tubulação de distribuição de oxigênio medicinal que atende o hospital.

O Hmib possui contrato regular de fornecimento de oxigênio medicinal e mantém uma central de backup com cilindros para situações como essa. A central foi acionada imediatamente, e os leitos afetados estão sendo abastecidos por cilindros, garantindo a continuidade da assistência aos pacientes internados.

A equipe técnica está no local realizando o reparo. A previsão é de que o serviço seja concluído e o fornecimento pela rede canalizada seja restabelecido ainda hoje (24/11)."

articles.title: Covid-19 em Divinópolis: casos sobem e vacinação de idosos preocupa | G1
articles.standfirst: Dos 406 casos confirmados neste ano, 332 foram registrados entre outubro e novembro. Município não registrou mortes pela doença em 2026. Em Itaúna, hospital tornou obrigatório o uso de máscaras.
articles.summary: Casos de covid-19 em Divinópolis dispararam no fim do ano e a baixa vacinação de idosos preocupa a saúde, enquanto hospital em Itaúna volta a exigir o uso de máscaras.
articles.body:

Divinópolis registrou 82% dos casos de covid-19 deste ano entre outubro e novembro. Dos 406 casos confirmados em 2026, 332 foram contabilizados nesses dois meses. Apesar do aumento, a cidade não registrou mortes pela doença neste ano .

O cenário preocupa também pela baixa cobertura vacinal entre idosos, gestantes e crianças. Segundo a Prefeitura, apenas 19% da população idosa está com a vacinação em dia, enquanto a cobertura recomendada é superior a 90%.

Na terça-feira (24), a Prefeitura informou que quatro escolas da rede municipal de ensino também registraram casos de covid-19 . A situação é acompanhada pelas equipes das secretarias municipais de Saúde e Educação.

Ainda de acordo com a administração municipal, o aumento de casos acompanha a tendência observada em Minas Gerais, com mais notificações de quadros leves e moderados da doença.

Em Itaúna , o Hospital Manoel Gonçalves tornou obrigatório o uso de máscaras nas dependências da unidade. A cidade confirmou 224 casos de covid-19 apenas nos primeiros 19 dias de novembro.

Até 12 de novembro, 17.434 doses da vacina contra a covid-19 foram aplicadas em Divinópolis. Entre os idosos, grupo com a menor cobertura vacinal, foram aplicadas 8.983 doses neste ano. A população com 60 anos ou mais na cidade é estimada em 47.157 pessoas. Veja os índices de cobertura vacinal:

A vacinação continua sendo a principal forma de proteção contra as formas graves da doença.

Segundo a Prefeitura, seguindo as orientações do Ministério da Saúde e da Secretaria de Estado de Saúde de Minas Gerais (SES-MG), a vacinação é indicada para os seguintes públicos:

crianças de 6 meses a menores de 5 anos: esquema de vacinação conforme o histórico vacinal, podendo incluir três doses.

população de 5 a 59 anos que nunca se vacinaram: dose única

idosos com 60 anos ou mais: uma dose a cada seis meses.

pessoas imunocomprometidas: vacinação semestral, conforme recomendações específicas.

grupos especiais, como profissionais de saúde, indígenas e quilombolas: reforço anual, conforme os critérios estabelecidos pelo Ministério da Saúde.

A orientação é que estes grupos procurem uma unidade de saúde para verificar a situação vacinal.

Hospital de Itaúna torna obrigatório o uso de máscaras

O Hospital Manoel Gonçalves, em Itaúna, divulgou na segunda-feira (23) uma nota técnica com medidas de proteção e controle de doenças respiratórias, entre elas a covid-19.

O uso de máscaras passou a ser obrigatório para profissionais, pacientes, acompanhantes e demais pessoas que circulam pelo hospital.

articles.title: Fetos de gêmeos foram incinerados sem autorização da família no Ceará | G1
articles.standfirst: O supervisor que autorizou a incineração sem ouvir a família e outros dois funcionários foram afastados. Em nota, o Hospital Regional do Sertão Central confirmou apenas o desaparecimento.
articles.summary: O supervisor que autorizou a incineração sem ouvir a família e outros dois funcionários foram afastados. Em nota, o Hospital Regional do Sertão Central confirmou apenas o desaparec
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Os fetos de dois bebês gêmeos , que morreram ainda durante a gestação, foram incinerados em um hospital do Ceará . No entanto, a família não autorizou a incineração . A informação foi repassada por uma fonte ouvida pelo g1 nesta quarta-feira (25).

Os fetos desapareceram após o parto realizado no último sábado (21), no Hospital Regional do Sertão Central (HRSC), em Quixeramobim , no interior do Ceará. Três funcionários do hospital — incluindo o supervisor que autorizou a incineração sem ouvir a família — foram afastados. Os nomes não foram divulgados.

A incineração dos fetos foi denunciada por familiares dos bebês. Segundo a advogada que os representa, a direção da unidade informou que os fetos haviam sido incinerados, mas não houve autorização da mãe .

Em nota oficial, o hospital confirmou que identificou o desaparecimento, mas não mencionou a incineração. No entanto, a fonte ouvida pelo g1 confirmou que os fetos foram incinerados.

A advogada da família, Luana Martins, informou que os familiares souberam do desaparecimento dos fetos na segunda-feira (23). No dia seguinte, receberam a informação de que os bebês haviam sido incinerados junto com outros resíduos hospitalares .

O HRSC informou que acionou imediatamente a Polícia Civil. O hospital também afirmou que afastou todos os envolvidos e iniciou procedimentos internos para apurar o caso . (Confira o posicionamento completo mais abaixo)

A Polícia Civil informou que a Delegacia de Polícia Civil de Quixeramobim instaurou inquérito policial para apurar o desaparecimento. A investigação segue em andamento, sob sigilo.

De acordo com a advogada da família, o caso começou em 20 de novembro, quando a mãe, grávida de 23 semanas, percebeu que os bebês não se movimentavam mais na barriga. Ela procurou uma Unidade Básica de Saúde (UBS) do município onde mora. Na unidade, os profissionais tentaram identificar os batimentos cardíacos dos bebês, mas não conseguiram.

A gestante foi encaminhada ao Hospital Regional do Sertão Central, onde passou por novos exames. Uma ultrassonografia confirmou que os dois bebês haviam morrido ainda no útero.

No dia 21 de novembro, Yasmin foi levada à sala de parto. Então, ela manifestou o desejo de realizar o velório e o sepultamento dos filhos. A mãe aguardava a liberação dos corpos, que haviam sido encaminhados para uma câmara fria do hospital.

Ao procurar informações sobre a liberação, no dia 23, a família foi informada de que os corpos não estavam no local. No dia seguinte, foi comunicada de que os corpos tinham sido incinerados junto com outros resíduos hospitalares.

Hospital Regional do Sertão Central está localizado em Quixeramobim. — Foto: Divulgação

Em nota, o Hospital Regional do Sertão Central (HRSC) informou que identificou o desaparecimento dos corpos de dois fetos gêmeos.

A unidade afirmou que a gestante foi encaminhada ao hospital por uma unidade de saúde do município de origem, onde a ausência de batimentos cardíacos já havia sido constatada. No HRSC, ela passou pelo procedimento obstétrico para a retirada dos fetos.

Ainda segundo o hospital, a direção acionou imediatamente a Polícia Civil e afastou todos os profissionais envolvidos . A unidade também informou que realiza procedimentos internos para esclarecer as circunstâncias da ocorrência, em colaboração com as autoridades responsáveis pela investigação.

O hospital manifestou solidariedade à família e afirmou que a mãe está sendo acompanhada pela equipe da unidade. A instituição reforçou o compromisso com a apuração dos fatos e com a colaboração às autoridades competentes.

"O Hospital Regional do Sertão Central (HRSC), unidade da Secretaria da Saúde do Ceará (Sesa), informa que identificou o desaparecimento dos corpos de dois fetos gêmeos. A gestante foi encaminhada ao HRSC pela unidade de saúde do município de origem, onde a ausência de batimentos cardíacos já havia sido constatada. No HRSC, ela passou pelo procedimento obstétrico para a retirada dos fetos.

A direção da unidade adotou todas as providências cabíveis, inclusive o acionamento imediato da Polícia Civil. Também afastou todos os envolvidos e realiza procedimentos internos para, em colaboração com autoridades responsáveis pela investigação, elucidar as circunstâncias da ocorrência.

O HRSC manifesta sua solidariedade e seu respeito à família, que está sendo acompanhada pela equipe da unidade.

O hospital reforça seu compromisso com a apuração rigorosa dos fatos e com a colaboração integral às autoridades competentes."

articles.title: FDA approves first new breast cancer hormone therapy in over two decades
articles.summary: Genentech says its oral drug Wilserdly reduced recurrence or death risk by 30% compared to standard endocrine therapy in the Phase III lidERA breast cancer trial.
articles.body: A new early-stage breast cancer therapy has been approved by the Food and Drug Administration for the first time in more than two decades. Wilserdly (giredestrant), an oral hormone therapy from San Francisco-based drugmaker Genentech, received the approval after positive trial results in treating adults with early-stage ER-positive, HER2-negative breast cancer. This subtype is the most common form of the disease in which tumor growth is fueled by the hormone estrogen rather than excess levels of the HER2 protein. NEW DRUG APPROACH OFFERS HOPE FOR PATIENTS WITH RECURRENT AGGRESSIVE CANCERS The Phase 3 lidERA study showed that the drug reduced the risk of disease recurrence or death by 30% compared to standard endocrine therapy, including generic pharmaceuticals like tamoxifen and aromatase inhibitors, according to a Genentech press release. Patients were also less likely to quit treatment because of side effects like joint pain and hot flashes compared to standard options, the researchers noted. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES The study found a reduction in cancer returning in distant parts of the body, like the bones, liver or lungs. Aditya Bardia, M.D., global principal investigator of the lidERA breast cancer trial and professor of medicine at the David Geffen School of Medicine at UCLA, noted that this finding is "particularly significant" because once breast cancer spreads to distant organs, it is "generally no longer curable." The foundational hormone therapies used for early-stage breast cancer have remained "largely unchanged" since the 2000s, Bardia told Fox News Digital. "These medicines have saved countless lives, but there has been room for improvement, both in terms of effectiveness and tolerability," he said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Now, for the first time in more than two decades, we have a new foundational hormone treatment that has been shown to be more effective than our existing standard therapies in early-stage breast cancer." Because most breast cancers are caught early and fall into the hormone receptor-positive subtype, the new therapy has the potential to help a large number of patients, Bardia added. Earlier this year, the FDA also approved Wilserdly combined with everolimus, an oral cancer medication, for the treatment of adults with ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer whose disease had recurred during or after completing endocrine-based therapy. This makes Wilserdly the "first and only" SERD (selective estrogen receptor degrader) that is FDA-approved to treat both early-stage and advanced ER-positive breast cancer. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Levi Garraway, M.D., chief medical officer and head of global product development, commented in a statement that the FDA approval is due to the drug showing "superior efficacy" against other therapies that have long been the standard of care. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Genentech, a member of the Roche Group, plans to continue investing in "broad development" of Wilserdly, exploring its potential across disease stages and in new treatment combinations, according to Roche Pharmaceuticals CEO Teresa Graham. Bardia encouraged patients to speak with their oncologists about the new treatment option, particularly those whose recent diagnosis is "consistent with the regulatory label and approval of the drug. articles.title: DU student found dead in Faridabad hotel, cops start murder probe despite suicide note
articles.summary: Delhi University student found dead in Faridabad hotel after checking in with neighbour; police file murder FIR despite suicide note, suspecting it was planted.
articles.body: GURGAON: A 19-year-old Delhi University student, who left home telling her parents she was going to college, was found dead in a Faridabad hotel room the next morning.She had checked in with a neighbour, who allegedly left during the night. Though police found a bottle of rat poison and a handwritten note in the room, they suspect the note may have been planted. A murder case has been registered.The woman, a second-year BCom student of Kalindi College, was found unconscious on a bed at Hotel Joya on Tuesday. The man she had checked in with lives directly opposite her house in Kureshipur village. Police are now searching for him.The sequence began on Monday morning, when she left home saying she was going to college. Her family remained in touch with her over phone till around 3pm, after which her mobile was switched off. When she did not return and repeated calls went unanswered, her family lodged a missing person’s complaint at Dhauj police station on Tuesday morning.A few hours later, cops at Sarai Khwaja police station informed the family that a woman had been found dead in a hotel room. They rushed there and identified her.Hotel staff told police that the two had checked in around 11am on Monday, submitting their own identity documents. The neighbour allegedly left during the night, while the student remained in the room. On Tuesday, staff knocked on the door to enquire if she would check out, but received no response. They then alerted police.The recovery of the handwritten note has added another layer to the case. Police said it mentioned pending monetary transactions. “Whatever is mine, Ankit will own it after me,” the note read, referring to the student’s brother.However, an officer said the handwriting did not appear to be hers and police suspected the note had been written by the neighbour to mislead them. Its origin and contents are being examined.The officer said the neighbour’s family runs a transport business, owning four to five trucks. Both his parents had died, and he frequently visited the student’s house and sometimes stayed there. Her parents run a grocery shop in the village.An FIR was registered under Section 103 of BNS (murder), besides the missing person’s case, at Dhauj police station. The body was sent to BK Hospital. The cause of death is yet to be established.“The autopsy will be carried out on Wednesday. articles.title: UK's oldest living heart transplant recipient dies aged 95
articles.summary: Ted Warner had a heart transplant in 1990 - and lived for another 36 years.
articles.body:
A man who was the UK's oldest living heart transplant recipient has died aged 95.

Ted Warner was 59 when he received the transplant from an anonymous donor at the Papworth Hospital in Cambridgeshire in 1990, and was only expected to live for eight more years.

But Warner lived for more than three decades before his death following a short illness on 7 November. Before his death, NHS officials confirmed he was the UK's oldest living heart transplant recipient and one of the oldest in the world.

His sons Neil and Adam told the BBC Warner, from Leicestershire, was a passionate advocate for organ donation. Neil added: "My dad always recognised that behind our joy was another family's tragedy."

Neil, 60, said: "We were blessed with an extra 36 years thanks to the transplanted heart.

"We are so grateful. He got to see his three grandchildren and enjoy so much of life."

Warner, who had been using a pacemaker, was told by a cardiologist at Leicester's Glenfield Hospital that he needed a heart transplant, following tests in January 1990.

However, he had to wait until August for a donor, not long after being told he had three weeks to live.

Warner, of Broughton Astley, said had he been just one year older, the operation would not have been allowed to go ahead - because of the greater risk to older recipients.

Papworth Hospital, which performed the UK's first successful heart transplant in 1979 , confirmed the expected survival rate was eight years at the time of Warner's operation.

Warner spoke to the BBC in 2021 as he celebrated his 90th birthday. At the time the hospital said Warner was the oldest person in the UK alive with a heart transplant.

Of his donor, he said: "I wrote a letter to their family many years ago and had a little bit of contact, but then they moved with no forwarding address and I could no longer reach them, but that's OK because it must have been so tough for them and what they were going through."

Another heart transplant recipient - Steve Syer, from Gloucestershire - was the UK's longest surviving single heart transplant patient, having lived for 38 years after his operation prior to his death in 2022 .

According to NHS Blood and Transplant, some heart transplants can only last for a few years "due to a number of factors", but "some go on to live over 30 years".

In 2025-26, it said 215 heart transplants took place in the UK.

Neil said: "There has never been a day since the transplant when my dad and our family have not been grateful for that generous gift of life."

Warner's loved ones understand that the donor was a young man, but they never learned of his identity.

"My dad always recognised that behind our joy was another family's tragedy," Neil added. "He never forgot that someone had died and that their family had made the extraordinary decision to donate his heart."

Warner retired from his textile equipment business, which is now run by his sons, but continued to lead an active life in later years.

He played golf, went clay pigeon shooting and regularly attended check-ups at the hospital, which has now moved sites and is called the Royal Papworth Hospital.

His other son Adam, 55, added: "It has been amazing for us.

"Dad got a second chance at life and seized the opportunity. He pretty much had two lives thanks to the donor."

Dr Doug Skehan, a retired NHS consultant cardiologist from Leicester's Glenfield Hospital, recalled first meeting Warner when he had a pacemaker fitted at the hospital in 1989.

He said: "Things were deteriorating, he was in some difficulty and the only way out was to consider a transplant.

"Ted is a fantastic advert for transplant surgery. He was also a strong supporter of charity golf competitions I organised."

Skehan said Warner's surgery was a successful result from a difficult situation.

"He's enjoyed life. The longevity of his transplant - 36 years is impressive," Skehan said.

"My message to people in celebrating Ted's life is to make sure your relatives know your wishes and views on organ donation.

"Saving lives relies on people being positive about it, so please give it your consideration."

An "opt-out" donation system was introduced in England in 2020, and presumes consent to donate organs for all adults unless they explicitly remove themselves from the list.

Following the heart transplant, his family said Warner often reflected on his second chance at life.

Speaking to the BBC previously, Warner said: "Most people take life for granted - and until you are about to lose it, you don't appreciate how valuable it is."

articles.title: CardAIology: Stroke risk to heart age, why ECG can now tell more than ever
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence is getting closer to our hearts, literally, one breakthrough at a time.
articles.body: Artificial intelligence is getting closer to our hearts, literally, one breakthrough at a time. From turning routine cardiac checkups into powerful early warning tools to speeding up emergency rescues during major heart attacks, AI is changing how doctors detect and treat heart disease both in the US and in India, where it is still the leading cause of death.“The biggest breakthrough is that the electrocardiogram (ECG) has become a new instrument,” shares Dr Afshine Emrani, a board-certified cardiologist who teaches at the UCLA’s David Geffen School of Medicine, US. “It’s a test that costs almost nothing and is done millions of times a year. AI now reads patterns in ECGs that no human eye can see: a heart attack hiding behind a ‘normal-looking’ tracing, a weakening heart muscle, a failing valve, even a heart ageing faster than its owner.”

articles.summary: Thiago Wall died in hospital three days after choking on food at the nursery, the inquest hears.
articles.body:
A three-year-old boy died after choking at a Greater Manchester nursery earlier this month, an inquest heard.

An inquest at Rochdale Coroner's Court heard on Wednesday that Thiago had choked on a bowl of food and died three days later at the Royal Manchester Children's Hospital. A CT scan later confirmed the toddler had suffered a brain injury.

The nursery - and three other nurseries owned by Cosy Toes LTD - remain closed.

The inquest heard the toddler had a hypoxic brain injury, which can be a result of decreased oxygen supply to the brain.

An investigation by Greater Manchester Police continues.

One tribute to Thiago left outside the nursery by other children read: "Thiago likes playing with the dinosaurs in nursery.

"We will always think of you Thiago, especially when we play dinosaurs."

articles.title: How skipping breakfast to save room for dinner shocks your blood sugar and metabolism
articles.summary: Dietitian Gabrielle Kishner warns that skipping breakfast before Thanksgiving causes blood sugar crashes, carb cravings and overeating at the holiday meal.
articles.body: Fasting all morning to save room for a big holiday feast might seem like a smart strategy, but experts say it can have unwanted health effects, and that there are better ways to prepare. When people go hours without food, blood sugar levels drop, triggering headaches, nausea and irritability, according to Gabrielle Kishner, a registered dietitian nutritionist and founder in New York City. "Once we get those uncomfortable symptoms of hunger, we're going to eat really fast when we get into Thanksgiving, because we're starving, " Kishner told Fox News Digital. "We're also going to crave more carbs and sugar to get that blood sugar back up." DOCTORS SETTLE DEBATE OVER DRINKING COFFEE ON AN EMPTY STOMACH AND POTENTIAL HEALTH RISKS Previous research has found that skipping daytime meals leads to significantly higher post-meal blood glucose spikes at dinner compared with eating regular meals. Regular breakfast omission has also been linked to disrupted circadian rhythms, impaired insulin sensitivity and a sluggish metabolism, as well as compensatory eating later in the day. To avoid coming to the dinner table starving, Kishner recommends eating a balanced breakfast within two hours of waking up and avoiding gaps of longer than four to six hours without food. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Combining carbohydrates, protein, fiber and healthy fats like Greek yogurt with berries and chia seeds, or avocado toast topped with hard-boiled eggs, helps stabilize energy and blood sugar so diners arrive "comfortably hungry, " she said. If the main meal takes place early in the afternoon, a balanced midmorning snack containing two nutrient groups, like vegetables and hummus, can help bridge the gap. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES How diners build that first plate also affects digestion and energy. Kishner recommends filling half the plate with fiber-rich fruits and vegetables, eating those first to slow digestion and help stabilize fullness. The second half of the plate should be split evenly between protein, like turkey, and carbohydrates, such as stuffing or mashed potatoes. Once the meal begins, pacing plays a major role in preventing gastrointestinal distress, Kishner said. Eating quickly makes it harder for the stomach to break down poorly chewed food, leading to bloating and discomfort. It takes roughly 20 to 30 minutes for the stomach to send satiety signals to the brain, meaning fast eaters often consume far more food than they need before realizing they are full, according to Cleveland Clinic. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Kishner recommends pausing midway through the meal to assess hunger levels, and waiting 10 to 20 minutes after finishing a plate before going back for seconds. Rich, creamy and sugary dishes take longer to digest, so sampling small portions from the dessert table helps to prevent stomachaches without making favorite foods off-limits. For those who do end up overindulging, gentle movement afterward can ease the post-meal slump. Kishner suggests taking a 10- to 15-minute walk with family or friends after the meal to aid digestion and blood sugar regulation. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Blood sugar typically peaks 30 to 90 minutes after a meal, and even brief, light-intensity walking helps blunt glucose spikes and keep insulin levels steady. Drinking water throughout the day also helps to digest food, according to Kishner. Above all, Kishner urges diners not to compensate the next morning by restricting food or skipping breakfast again, which only restarts the cycle of blood sugar crashes and overeating.

articles.title: Israeli strike in Gaza kills senior Hamas official, his wife and children
articles.summary: Gaza’s internal security director and his family are among seven Palestinians killed in one day by Israeli forces.
articles.body:
Israeli attacks on Gaza have killed at least seven Palestinians, including a senior security official, according to medical sources and local officials.

In a statement on Wednesday, Gaza’s Interior Ministry said Muhammad Majid Abu al-Awf, director of the Internal Security Service in northern Gaza, was killed in an attack on Shati refugee camp. Al-Awf’s wife and two daughters, aged 13 and 15, were also killed, it added.

The ministry described the killings as a “horrific massacre perpetrated by the Israeli occupation forces when they bombed [the family’s] residence in the Shati refugee camp” in Gaza City.

The attack is part of “ongoing attempts to undermine the security apparatus in the Gaza Strip in an effort to spread chaos within Palestinian society”, it added.

A source at al-Shifa Hospital confirmed to Al Jazeera that four people from the same family were killed and several were wounded in an Israeli attack on an apartment in the refugee camp.

The attack came less than 24 hours after the killing of the Internal Security Service’s director general, Brigadier-General Naim Abu Nahal.

In another deadly incident, two Palestinians were killed in a drone attack on the al-Karama neighbourhood in Gaza City while a seventh Palestinian man was killed when an Israeli attack hit a tent sheltering displaced people in Jabalia al-Balad in northern Gaza.

Medical sources at the Nasser Medical Complex reported that a Palestinian girl was injured when she was shot by Israeli forces in areas outside their control in Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip.

Near-daily Israeli violations of a “ceasefire” in Gaza have been recorded since it began in October 2025. Israeli air attacks regularly hit the enclave, and at least 1,680 people have been killed during the “ceasefire” and more than 6,000 injured as Israel’s genocidal war continues.

Hamas called on the guarantor states of the “ceasefire” to intervene immediately “to rein in the occupation, impose a halt to its crimes and obligate it to adhere to the agreement’s path”.

articles.title: Fans With Limb Differences Share Emotional Reactions to Ezra Frech’s ‘DWTS’ Win After His Prosthetic Fell Off
articles.summary: Ezra Frech is being celebrated by members of the limb difference community for winning his “Dancing With the Stars” season.
articles.body: Ezra Frech is being celebrated by members of the limb difference community for winning his “Dancing With the Stars” season, after a tricky finale performance where his prosthetic leg came off. The Paralympic gold medalist, 21, and his pro partner Daniella Karagach were crowned the Season 35 champions on the Nov. 24 episode, making Frech the first Paralympian and amputee to win the coveted Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy. The duo’s 11 weeks of stellar dances hit a glitch during the finale when, midway through their freestyle routine, Frech’s prosthetic leg was accidentally knocked off by fellow dancers who lifted him to a lower part of the stage. What happened next was an unscripted dramatic moment made for TV. The unflappable Frech, now dancing on one leg, was able to pull off his own lift of Karagach before pro dancer Alan Bersten retrieved his prosthetic and handed it back to him. Frech swiftly reattached his prosthetic, rubbed his hands together and finished the dance to wild cheers. “I haven’t watched the video back, but you can see I’m fidgeting with it as I’m running up. ... Sometimes it will lock into place even if it’s not on right, so I had to just go, and then when I jumped, I was like, ‘Oh my God, it’s going to come off.’ And then it came off. Everything happened so fast,” Frech told Extra TV after the finale. “I was prepared to dance the rest of the dance on one leg if I had to. But (Karagach) yelled, ‘Put on your leg!’ and I heard that, and I blacked out, and I don’t know what happened,” added the track star, who won gold medals in both the 100 meter and the high jump at the 2024 Paris Paralympics. Frech’s victory, as well as his remarkable grace under pressure, are being applauded by members of the limb difference community. Frech was born without a left knee and shin bone, and with one finger on his left hand, according to his website. At age 2, his left leg was amputated and a toe was transplanted to his left hand. He started using his first prosthetic leg at 11 months old and his first running blade at age 4. “I can promise you that you made more than one person with a disability feel more confident @EzraFrech,” one woman captioned a TikTok video of her cheering while watching the athlete dance. “No better feeling than watching someone else with a limb difference win Dancing With the Stars.” Parents of young children with limb difference also celebrated Frech’s win. “No words can touch how empowering this is for her, and how much it has filled my heart with gratitude,” wrote one father on Instagram, who shared a video of his young daughter celebrating Frech’s win. “You have impacted my daughter’s life,” he continued, tagging Frech, “and I know she will carry this moment, this whole season with her forever.

articles.title: A Dietitian Shares the No. 1 Unhealthy Habit You Should Avoid this Thanksgiving
articles.summary: A dietitian shares the top unhealthy habit she wants people to avoid on Thanksgiving and what to do instead.
articles.body: Thanksgiving is all about enjoying delicious foods. Still, every year ahead of this cooking-centric day, you’ll come across people or content suggesting you do the opposite. “I always see people not eating all day to ‘save up’ calories for the big feast, or feeling like they have to do a Turkey Trot the morning of Thanksgiving to negate the calories they’re going to eat,” says Natalie Rizzo, dietitian and TODAY.com nutrition editor. If you’re worried about maintaining your health or nutrition goals on Thanksgiving, you’re not alone. But there’s only one thing Rizzo actually recommends avoiding — and it has nothing to do with calories, saturated fat or sugar. Avoid Feeling Guilty for Eating Foods You Love “The main thing I want people to avoid on Thanksgiving is feeling any guilt associated with eating foods you love,” says Rizzo. Food guilt often occurs when we assign morality to foods, labeling them as either “good” or “bad.” As a result, this can spur negative self-talk about our eating habits, says Rizzo. “People will say they are ‘being bad’ on Thanksgiving by eating all the indulgent foods,” Rizzo adds. But even if your Thanksgiving favorites have less nutritional value than your usual diet, you can still enjoy them. Thanksgiving comes once a year! “Remember that one day does not make or break your health goals. It’s the little things we do on a daily basis that really contribute to our health,” explains Rizzo. Feeling ashamed after eating certain “off-limits” foods can lead to an unhealthy cycle of restricting and overeating. Plus, it can trigger stress and put a real damper on your holiday. “If you love sitting around the table with family and eating pumpkin pie, then you should do that without guilt,” says Rizzo. Ultimately, Thanksgiving is more about enjoying a nice meal and time with loved ones (or yourself) than anything else. What to Do Instead As a dietitian, Rizzo firmly believes that people should “eat whatever the heck they want” on Thanksgiving Day, which includes breakfast or lunch before the main meal. Whether it’s your grandma’s stuffing or your aunt’s macaroni and cheese, load up and try to savor the flavors. Thanksgiving dishes often hold traditions and memories, which is even more reason to enjoy them. After the meal, you may find yourself in food coma, but don’t panic. “If you do overeat and feel crappy, remember that it’s a fleeting feeling and will eventually subside,” says Rizzo. However, there are things you can do to feel better in the moment and aid digestion. First, make sure to drink plenty of water throughout the day to stay hydrated, Rizzo emphasizes. After finishing your meal, Rizzo recommends going on a 10–20 minute walk. “Holiday meals tend to be very fatty and salty, and water and movement keeps the digestive system moving and may reduce some of the indigestion,” says Rizzo. A post-meal walk can help speed up intestinal motility and relieve trapped gas, easing uncomfortable bloating. Walking can also help stabilize blood sugar, which tends to spike after a big meal. If you can’t get out for a walk, try moving your body in another way, like clearing the table or washing dishes. “I also think it’s important to remember how you feel when you overeat as a reminder to try to eat more balanced meals in the future,” says Rizzo. In the days following Thanksgiving, try to eat nutrient-dense foods at your usual meal times to get back into a routine — but don’t feel guilty about eating the leftovers. If you still feel backed up, increase your fiber intake by eating more vegetables, fruits and legumes. The National Alliance for Eating Disorders Helpline provides support, resources and information about treatment options at 1-866-662-1235, Monday through Friday.

articles.title: 22-year-old beaten to death by friends for trying to cut ties following daughter’s birth in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Bengaluru: 22-year-old lift repair worker Ambar was allegedly beaten to death by friends after cutting ties post daughter’s birth; three arrested, police say internal bleeding caused death.
articles.body: BENGALURU: A 22-year-old man, who reportedly wanted to turn over a new leaf after becoming a father, was allegedly beaten to death by his friends after deciding to cut ties with them. His family has accused the group of repeatedly assaulting and threatening him, and demanding that he meet them whenever they summoned him.The deceased, Ambar, a resident of Horamavu, worked in lift repair. Originally from Nepal, his family had moved to Bengaluru 25 years ago. Ambar married Pooja Chhetri in 2024, and the couple welcomed a baby girl about a week before his death.Ambar’s elder brother, Nagaraj, told police that Ambar was close to Syed Yunus, a resident of Shampura Road, and his associates. Yunus frequently visited their house to take Ambar along. Ambar often spent considerable time with the group and sometimes stayed away from home for a day or two.Nagaraj said Ambar had repeatedly told the family that Yunus, Junaid alias Koli and their associates would assault and intimidate him over minor disagreements. In October, the group allegedly assaulted him, injuring his left arm. Although the family suggested filing a police complaint, Ambar refused, saying the accused were his friends.After the birth of his daughter, Ambar reportedly told his friends that he no longer wished to associate with them. However, Yunus and Junaid allegedly assaulted and threatened him, insisting that he meet them whenever they summoned him.On Nov 18, around 5am, Ambar brought milk and biscuits home, told his mother that he had some work and left on his motorcycle. He did not return. When relatives tried calling him and Yunus, both their phones were switched off. After searching for him for two days, the family decided to approach Hennur police.On Nov 23, the family received a call from DJ Halli police asking them to rush to Ambedkar Hospital, where they learnt that Ambar had died.Body found in fourth-floor storeroomThe family learnt that Mohammed Shafi, 61, father of Syed Yunus, had found Ambar’s body in a storeroom on the fourth floor of his residence in Muneshwaranagar on November 22. Shafi approached the police and sought a post-mortem examination to establish the cause of death. DJ Halli police registered an unnatural death report.During the examination of the body, police noticed bleeding injuries on both arms, the right leg, the face near the eye and several parts of the head and body, raising suspicions of an assault.Nagaraj alleged that Yunus, Junaid alias Koli and their associates had taken Ambar to a room above Yunus’s house, confined him and assaulted him with an object on his right leg, face, head and other parts of the body. The injuries allegedly led to his death.A senior police officer said, “We have arrested Tamheem , 23, Md Mudasir, 22 and Yunus, 24. articles.title: Doctors warn of lead exposure health risks after controversial Army detonation in Iowa
articles.summary: The Army detonated five tons of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant, and FEMA says residents within 20 miles must shelter until the all clear.
articles.body: The U.S. Army blew up about five tons of lead azide, a toxic bomb-making chemical, in a controlled detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown on Wednesday, raising concerns over airborne heavy-metal exposure. The mission was reportedly necessary because the substances were "unstable" and liable to explode if tampered with. While a Trump administration official reported that the detonation exceeded expectations by achieving maximum mitigation, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) warned that residents within 20 miles should continue to shelter in place to avoid inhaling lead dust, and should follow EPA safety guidance "until given the all clear by officials." IOWA RESIDENTS NEAR AMMUNITION PLANT TOLD TO VACATE BEFORE ARMY DETONATES 5 TONS OF BOMB-MAKING CHEMICALS "[The] EPA has been on the ground in Iowa BEFORE the controlled detonation, we will be here DURING the detonation, and we will be here for as long as necessary AFTER detonation to ensure communities are safe," the Environmental Protection Agency said prior to the blast. The agency predicted a brief increase in lead in the air above Middletown, as officials in Iowa and Missouri warned of potential exposure to toxic lead dust. According to Mayo Clinic, even small amounts of lead can cause serious health problems. Long-term buildup of lead in the body can get stored and slowly re-enter the bloodstream over time. AGGRESSIVE CANCER TYPE LINKED TO COMMON CHEMICAL EXPOSURE IN NEW STUDY At very high levels, lead can damage the kidneys and nervous system in both children and adults, leading to complications in the brain, seizures, neuropsychiatric symptoms and unconsciousness. Children under 6 years old are the most susceptible, as lead poisoning can severely impact development of their bodies and brains. According to the Iowa Farm Bureau, Iowa leads the nation in producing corn, pigs, eggs, ethanol and biodiesel — commodities that end up in everyday household products." The state also ranks No. 2 in soybean production and cover crops. One Iowa farmer, Doug Seyb, spoke with PBS about his concern that the detonation could impact his nearby farm, including his cows out at pasture and local ponds that fill the farm's water tank. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES The public fears that lead could eventually enter the food supply through crops grown in contaminated soil and livestock raised on contaminated water. Dr. Stephanie Widmer, New York City emergency medicine physician, medical toxicologist and Fox News medical contributor, confirmed that lead being dispersed into the air is "not a small deal." "Lead has no beneficial role in human physiology," she said. "In fact, lead in the human body can really mess with biology." People who eat fresh produce already take in trace amounts of heavy metals like lead, which is widespread in soil — but detonating a "tremendous amount" of the toxic metal raises the risk of dangerous exposure, Widmer warned. AGGRESSIVE CANCER TYPE LINKED TO COMMON CHEMICAL EXPOSURE IN NEW STUDY "If there is an enormous amount that is going to be contaminating the food supply, the water, the air that people are breathing in, this is very concerning," she said. Widmer suggested that Americans near the detonation site should continue to listen to guidance to shelter in place, keep windows closed, and turn on ventilation or air purifying systems. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "We know that lead is dangerous for humans, but we don't know how much, or if any, lead they're being exposed to," she said. "It could be none. It could a ton." The EPA reported no levels of lead in the air 30 minutes after the detonation, but Widmer noted that just because the blow is over doesn't mean there is no lingering impact. "Lead inhalation is one of the most efficient ways that lead can be dispersed into the human body," she said, adding that even if it's not inhaled, it can be dispersed into the soil. "It can stay in soil, it could stay in water," the doctor said. "The very concerning thing is that lead can have negative effects on the human body without even showing any symptoms," she said. articles.title: CEDIM terá novo tomógrafo com inteligência artificial | G1
articles.standfirst: Equipamento Philips CT 5300 reúne inteligência artificial, imagens de alta qualidade e recursos para exames cardíacos em Cacoal e região.
articles.summary: Equipamento Philips CT 5300 reúne inteligência artificial, imagens de alta qualidade e recursos para exames cardíacos em Cacoal e região.
articles.body:
Imagem ilustrativa do Philips CT 5300, novo equipamento de tomografia computadorizada que será incorporado à estrutura do CEDIM. — Foto: Divulgação

O CEDIM – Centro de Diagnóstico por Imagem está se preparando para receber o Philips CT 5300 , um novo equipamento de tomografia computadorizada que incorpora recursos avançados de inteligência artificial e tecnologias desenvolvidas para melhorar a qualidade das imagens e ampliar as possibilidades de investigação médica.

A novidade representa mais um investimento do CEDIM em tecnologia para o diagnóstico por imagem, fortalecendo a estrutura oferecida à população de Cacoal e região.

Um dos grandes diferenciais do equipamento é a inteligência artificial aplicada em diferentes etapas do exame. Essa tecnologia auxilia em processos como o posicionamento do paciente e a organização da aquisição das imagens, contribuindo para um fluxo de realização mais ágil e padronizado.

O equipamento conta com uma câmera inteligente que auxilia no posicionamento do paciente, ajudando a tornar essa etapa mais consistente e eficiente. Além disso, ferramentas de automação contribuem para otimizar processos que fazem parte da rotina da tomografia.

Imagens de alta qualidade, inclusive para exames do coração

Outro destaque do Philips CT 5300 está na tecnologia utilizada para produzir imagens com mais detalhes, inclusive em avaliações de estruturas que apresentam movimento constante, como o coração.

Durante uma tomografia cardíaca, o movimento do coração pode representar um desafio para a obtenção das imagens. Por isso, o equipamento conta com recursos específicos que ajudam a compensar esse movimento e melhorar a visualização das artérias coronárias.

Essa tecnologia amplia os recursos disponíveis para a investigação cardiovascular, fornecendo imagens que auxiliam o médico na avaliação de possíveis alterações e na definição das condutas necessárias para cada paciente.

Tecnologia para otimizar a dose de radiação

Outro aspecto importante é a presença de recursos desenvolvidos para melhorar a qualidade das imagens com otimização da dose de radiação.

O sistema combina um detector avançado com inteligência artificial para reconstruir as imagens, permitindo trabalhar com doses reduzidas em determinadas situações, mantendo a qualidade necessária para a avaliação diagnóstica.

A dose utilizada é definida de acordo com o tipo de exame, a região do corpo analisada e as características de cada paciente, seguindo os critérios técnicos e os protocolos estabelecidos.

Mais possibilidades para o diagnóstico em Cacoal e região

A chegada do Philips CT 5300 representa mais um avanço na estrutura tecnológica do CEDIM. O equipamento foi desenvolvido para diferentes aplicações da tomografia computadorizada, incluindo avaliações cardíacas, exames em situações de trauma e procedimentos intervencionistas.

Com essa aquisição, o CEDIM reforça seu investimento em inovação e na ampliação dos recursos disponíveis para a investigação diagnóstica na região.

A tecnologia tem um papel importante na medicina, mas seu aproveitamento depende também do conhecimento dos profissionais que conduzem os exames e interpretam as informações obtidas. É essa integração que contribui para oferecer um suporte cada vez mais completo à avaliação médica.

Mais tecnologia, inteligência artificial e novas possibilidades para o diagnóstico por imagem. É assim que o CEDIM continua acompanhando a evolução da medicina diagnóstica e investindo em recursos para cuidar da saúde de Cacoal e região.

O equipamento tem previsão de chegada ao CEDIM ainda em 2026. Acompanhe os canais oficiais da clínica para conhecer as novidades e as informações sobre a disponibilização dos exames.

articles.standfirst: Segundo a Prefeitura de Humaitá, o homem foi identificado como Carlos Luciano dos Santos Negrão. Ele está internado no hospital do município, onde recebe atendimento médico e psiquiátrico.
articles.summary: Após ser encontrado na BR-319, Carlos Luciano dos Santos Negrão foi resgatado em Humaitá e segue internado para receber cuidados médicos e psiquiátricos.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Carlos Luciano dos Santos Negrão, de 56 anos, natural de São Paulo , foi resgatado na manhã de quarta-feira (25), após passar 27 dias desaparecido em uma área de mata às margens da BR-319, em Humaitá , no sul do Amazonas. Ele foi encontrado sem roupas e debilitado por trabalhadores de uma empresa que atua na região e precisou ser retirado pelos bombeiros de um trecho de difícil acesso.

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Amazonas (CBMAM), Carlos foi localizado na altura do km 70 da rodovia, no sentido Porto Velho (RO). A equipe do 7º Grupamento de Bombeiros Militar (GBM) foi acionada pela Polícia Militar e chegou ao local cerca de 40 minutos depois.

Os militares precisaram entrar na mata para alcançar o homem, que apresentava sinais de fraqueza . Para retirá-lo com segurança, utilizaram uma prancha rígida e uma maca tipo cesto.

Depois de chegar a um local seguro, Carlos foi aquecido com uma manta térmica e teve os sinais vitais avaliados pelos bombeiros.

Após os primeiros socorros, ele foi levado de ambulância para o Hospital Regional de Humaitá, onde permanece internado.

Segundo informações da Prefeitura de Humaitá, o paciente recebe assistência médica e psiquiátrica. A unidade hospitalar identificou que ele é do estado paulista e tem histórico de acompanhamento psiquiátrico.

As circunstâncias de como Carlos foi parar na área de mata não foram divulgadas.

articles.title: Taking Ozempic or Wegovy could lead to extra cancer screenings, new study suggests
articles.summary: A study for the Radiological Society of North America links GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy to higher breast density on mammograms in 62.5% of women.
articles.body: Women taking popular weight loss medications may have higher breast density on mammograms and require more follow-up imaging, even when none of those abnormalities turn out to be cancer. That's according to a new study scheduled for presentation at the annual meeting of the Radiological Society of North America, Nov. 29-Dec. 3, 2026, in Chicago. The study examined 107 women, ages 34 to 79, who took GLP-1 receptor agonists, a class of drugs that includes Ozempic and Wegovy, for weight loss for at least one year. POPULAR WEIGHT LOSS DRUGS MAY PLAY SURPRISING ROLE IN CANCER OUTCOMES Participants lost between six and 107 pounds, with an average loss of 40 pounds. Researchers reviewed 214 screening mammograms taken before and after at least a year of treatment, according to the study. Specialized software showed that breast density rose by at least one category in 62.5% of participants who took GLP-1s. Eight women moved up two density categories. Radiologists also saw smaller breasts in roughly 58% to 79% of patients, depending on the reviewer, and increased skin thickening in about 9% to 18%. Higher breast density is generally tied to a greater risk of breast cancer and can make tumors harder to spot on X-rays. However, the pattern seen after weight loss likely reflects a shift in proportions rather than more dense tissue growing, according to lead author Dr. Eva C. Gombos, a diagnostic radiologist at Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston. POPULAR WEIGHT LOSS DRUGS MAY HELP PROTECT AGAINST A DEADLY DISEASE, DOCTOR SAYS "It was surprising that 62.5% of women had increased BI-RADS breast density despite substantial weight loss, with no decreases observed," Gombos said in a release. "This may reflect disproportionate loss of breast fat, causing a relative increase in mammographic density even as absolute fibroglandular volume decreases." When a person loses significant fat from the breast, the remaining milk ducts and supportive tissue — known as fibroglandular tissue — can make up a larger share of what shows up on the image, even if the total amount of that tissue did not grow. Gombos also noted that losing breast fat and volume can leave extra skin or skin folds, which may help explain why skin and connective tissue strands looked more prominent on some scans. Nearly 22.4% of the women were called back for additional imaging after screening, compared with an average U.S. recall rate of about 10%. Two women had technical recalls to repeat scans due to positioning or imaging issues. Four women were referred for biopsies, and all four came back benign. All other callbacks also turned out to be benign or negative, including three simple cysts. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES Gombos emphasized that the findings should not pose a concern for women taking GLP-1 drugs or cause them to skip routine screenings. Whether these density shifts carry any long-term change in breast cancer risk remains unclear and needs more research. TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The study was retrospective and looked back at medical records rather than following patients forward in a controlled trial, the researchers noted. It did not establish whether the imaging changes affect long-term breast cancer risk. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER Gombos recommends that women tell their breast imaging team if they use GLP-1 medications or have recently lost a significant amount of weight because it helps technologists and radiologists more accurately compare new scans to older ones. Novo Nordisk, maker of Ozempic and Wegovy, emphasized that it continuously monitors the safety profile of its medicines, reviewing emerging data as it becomes available. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Individuals respond to treatment uniquely based on multiple biological and lifestyle factors, which means outcomes can vary from person to person," a spokesperson told Fox News Digital. "We recommend that all patients maintain close contact with their healthcare professional to discuss any questions or concerns about their treatment, and for ongoing guidance and careful monitoring."

articles.body: GHAZIABAD: A 42-year-old woman was arrested for allegedly trying to slow-poison her husband, son and nephew at their house in Vasundhara by spiking their food with small doses of lead regularly over a period of at least 12 months.Renu, who was arrested on Nov 23, has allegedly revealed during interrogation she wanted full control of her husband's transport business, which currently has an annual turnover of around Rs 6 crore.Police said Renu was taken into custody from her sister's house in Delhi's Jhilmil Colony after a preliminary investigation following an FIR in Sept based on a complaint by Sushil Kumar Bhatnagar (45), her husband. In his complaint, Bhatnagar claimed he had fallen severely ill on Aug 21 last year, and tests done at a private facility showed high levels of lead in his blood samples. He remained admitted at Max Hospital in Vaishali for two months.Bhatnagar told police he fell ill again later that year and was admitted to hospital for a second time. Doctors diagnosed him with chronic lead poisoning. He said his 16-year-old son Vansh and 21-year-old nephew Dev Bhatnagar also took ill over the next few months and recovery took weeks. DCP trans-Hindon Rijul said Bhatnagar began to suspect Renu when medical reports of all three victims showed lead poisoning.6cr biz, 2cr insurance: Money, control motives in poisoning plotDCP trans-Hindon Rijul told TOI Bhatnagar began to suspect Renu when medical reports of all three victims showed lead poisoning. "Bhatnagar, however, did not have any evidence at the time. He told police that in the first week of Sept this year, his 12-year-old daughter told him Renu would set aside portions for the mother-daughter before 'spraying something on the food' she served to the rest of the family," the DCP said.When Bhatnagar confronted Renu, she allegedly didn't respond and instead went to his sister's house in Delhi. On Sept 24, Bhatnagar submitted a complaint at Indirapuram police station. An FIR was registered against Renu under BNS sections 109 (attempt to murder), 123 (causing hurt by poison or drugs) and 61 (2) (criminal conspiracy). Four others, including her mother Lata Saxena, her brother Ravi, her brother-in-law Sushil Girdhar and an acquaintance Bablu, were also named in the FIR for conniving."Police recorded the statement of the girl, doctors and reviewed the reports of the three victims. After initial investigation, police found substantial evidence that Renu was administering poison to her husband, son and nephew between 2024 and 2025," the DCP said.After her arrest, Renu is said to have told police she mixed lead in small quantities in the food she served to her husband, son and nephew. "Renu claimed she wanted to take over his travel agency. So, she decided to kill Bhatnagar and nephew Dev, who is the caretaker of the business. Renu also tried to kill her son as he backed his father," Rijul said. Renu was also the nominee for Bhatnagar's life insurance policy worth Rs 2 crore.The DCP said police are trying to determine where the woman bought the poison or if someone gave it to her. Police are also investigating whether others were involved. She threw the poison into a trash bin somewhere before leaving her husband's house in Sept, a police officer said.According to doctors, chronic lead poisoning often causes no obvious early symptoms even as lead builds up in the body and harms organs. When symptoms appear over weeks, months or years, they vary by age and commonly affect the digestive, nervous, cardiovascular and reproductive systems. "Lead poisoning can cause death if exposure is severe or treatment is delayed. Extremely high levels of lead can cause seizures, coma and permanent brain damage," said Dr Sanjay Teotia, former CMS of Sanjay Nagar Hospital in Ghaziabad.The case has similarities with Keralam's Koodathayi cyanide murder case, where a woman, Jolly Joseph, was accused of killing six members of her family between 2002 and 2016.The victims included her mother-in-law Annamma Thomas, father-in-law Tom Thomas, first husband Roy Thomas, Annamma's brother Mathew Manjadiyil, and Sily and her two-year-old daughter Alphine. Investigators alleged that Joseph used cyanide, mixed with food or drinks, to poison five victims. She allegedly used veterinary poison, sold as 'dog kill', to murder Annamma. Police suspected property disputes and her desire to marry Sily's husband as motives. Arrested in Oct 2019, Joseph faces six murder cases. articles.title: Note found in Faridabad hotel confirms DU student was killed, boyfriend says ‘tired of the world’
articles.summary: Faridabad hotel note says 19-year-old DU student Arna Singh was killed by boyfriend Vipin Yadav; police register murder case and launch search for absconding man.
articles.body: GURGAON: A note found in the Faridabad hotel room where a 19-year-old DU student was found dead on Tuesday indicated she was murdered by the youth she was in a relationship with, police said. Her boyfriend — who had checked out before police arrived — left two notes, in one of which he confessed to killing her and said he would die by suicide too. Vipin Yadav, 26, claimed the two had been in a relationship for eight years and the decision had been made by both as they were “tired of the world”. Police have launched a search operation for him.Arna Singh, a second-year BCom student at Delhi University’s Kalindi College, was found dead on Tuesday morning in a room at Hotel Joya in Faridabad’s Sector 37. The two notes, written by Vipin, and a bottle of rat poison were recovered from the room, police said.In the first note, Vipin wrote that the decision to end their lives had been taken by both of them. “I, Vipin Yadav and Arna have been in love with each other for the last eight years and are tired of the world. Because of this, we are taking this step. I have killed her and then I will kill myself,” the note stated.He further claimed he had attempted suicide three to four times earlier but had been saved. “This is why I am going to the canal and have shared my last location on Arna’s phone,” the note stated.Police said he had only written about sharing his location and had not actually sent it. “The note does not mention a specific location for the canal, and he did not send any location to Arna’s phone,” a senior police officer said. Police are trying to trace Vipin’s movements and phone location, including whether he travelled elsewhere after leaving the hotel.The second note written by Vipin contained details of monetary transactions and the names of people with whom he had pending financial settlements, with amounts to be received from or paid to different people. The officer said the entries appeared to range from Rs 50,000 to Rs 3,50,000 to be received, along with transactions with people he had to pay or had already paid.“One of the transactions he had mentioned in the note was with a person to whom he had paid Rs 1 lakh in the morning before they had checked into the hotel,” the officer added.The notes have become an important part of the murder investigation. “We are examining the authenticity of the handwritten notes. The crime and the forensics team have taken evidences from the hotel room, which are being analysed,” the police officer said.Police said the two checked into the hotel between 9.45am and 10am on Monday. According to the inquiry, Vipin left around 10.30 pm. “We have taken the hotel’s CCTV footage into possession and are examining it thoroughly to establish their movements inside and outside the premises,” another officer said. Hotel staff who knocked on the door the next morning to clean the room received no response, after which police were alerted.Arna had left her home in Kureshipur on Monday morning, telling her parents she was going to college. Her family stayed in touch with her by phone until around 3pm, after which her phone was switched off. When she failed to return and repeated calls went unanswered, the family lodged a missing-person complaint at Dhauj police station on Tuesday morning. A few hours later, Sarai Khwaja police informed them that a woman had been found dead in a hotel room. The family rushed to the hotel and identified her.“Vipin, who lived opposite Arna’s house in the village, was known to her family and frequently visited their home. He had also eaten meals at their house on several occasions,” the officer said.An FIR was registered against Vipin at Dhauj police station on Tuesday under BNS Section 103 (murder). “The body was sent to BK Hospital for a postmortem examination. articles.title: Bengaluru hospital's CPAP machine overheats to 69 degrees, burns 29-week premature baby's nose within 27 hours of birth; consumer court orders hospital to pay Rs 40 lakh for lifelong injuries
articles.summary: BENGALURU: A consumer commission in Bengaluru has directed a government medical college and hospital to pay Rs 40 lakh in compensation to the mother of a
articles.body: BENGALURU: A consumer commission in Bengaluru has directed a government medical college and hospital to pay Rs 40 lakh in compensation to the mother of a premature baby girl who suffered severe burns to her nose after a medical device overheated in the hospital's neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) in 2022.The commission held ESIC Medical College and Hospital in Rajajinagar, its dean, chief medical officer and the then NICU in-charge responsible for medical negligence and deficiency in service. In its November 4 order, the commission, headed by president Syed Anser Kaleem, said the hospital could not avoid liability by blaming a manufacturing defect in the equipment.The complaint said the woman, a resident of JP Nagar, delivered the baby girl through an emergency caesarean section on August 18, 2022. The child was born at 29 weeks and three days of gestation, weighing 1.22 kg. The newborn was diagnosed with severe Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) and placed on a Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) machine to support her breathing, according to the complaint.However, about 27 hours after her birth, the machine's thermostat and humidifier allegedly malfunctioned, causing its temperature to rise to between 52 and 69 degrees Celsius. Flames and fumes reportedly emerged from the equipment. The baby suffered severe burns to her nose and was shifted to Narayana Hrudayalaya on August 19, 2022, for advanced treatment. She remained under treatment for 90 days, the order said.The mother told the commission that the injuries had left the child, now two years old, with permanent nasal disfigurement and severe black scarring. She said the girl would require extensive medical interventions in the future, including nasal debridement and planned nasal reconstruction. The child had also developed permanent patchy hair loss in a specific region, the complaint stated.The hospital, however, argued that the four-year-old CPAP machine was covered by a comprehensive maintenance contract and had been certified as functioning normally during its last preventive maintenance check in March 2022. It contended that the equipment had failed due to a manufacturing defect and that it had provided the necessary treatment and follow-up care, including bearing the expenses of the child's 90-day hospitalisation at Narayana Hrudayalaya.The hospital also said it had terminated the use of all medical devices manufactured by the company concerned across its facilities and blacklisted the manufacturer, stopping any future procurement of its products. The commission said the hospital had a responsibility to ensure that medical equipment used on a vulnerable newborn was safe and properly monitored. It held that the hospital could not escape liability by attributing the incident to a manufacturing defect."For a CPAP machine to overheat to the extent of producing visible flames and fumes inside an infant's nasal passage implies a profound breakdown of active institutional monitoring," it said.Taking note of the child's permanent injuries and the need for future medical treatment, the commission directed the hospital and the three officials to jointly and severally pay Rs 40 lakh in compensation, along with interest at six per cent per annum from the date of filing the complaint until the amount is realised. The commission said the injuries would have lifelong consequences for the child."Any amount of compensation cannot bring back the originality of the child and the child has to suffer lifelong." It also directed that the compensation be deposited in a long-term fixed deposit in a nationalised bank in the minor's name until she attains majority. The mother will be allowed to withdraw the quarterly interest for the child's medical expenses and welfare, the order said.(With inputs from PTI)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news.
