articles.title: Royal Berkshire Hospital to replace artwork with direction signage
articles.summary: A local artist says the decision will make the hospital feel more "clinical and depressing".
articles.body:
The planned removal of artwork from hospital corridors has disappointed an artist who says the displays bring comfort to patients and visitors.

Michelle Martin, from Shinfield, said she had been told the Royal Berkshire Hospital in Reading would stop exhibiting work by local artists in 2027.

She said that the decision would make the hospital feel more "clinical and depressing", adding that artwork sales also raised money for its charity.

Royal Berkshire NHS Foundation Trust said it wanted to improve the experience of patients and visitors by using the space to help people find their way around, but was exploring alternative areas for artwork.

Martin, who creates mandalas, said she had applied several times to have her work displayed at the hospital.

She explained that artists put up their own work, with 25% of any sales going to the hospital charity.

Speaking to BBC Radio Berkshire's Vernon Harwood , she said the artwork offered a welcome distraction for people visiting the hospital, often during difficult times.

"They'd had experiences either through having treatment or sadly losing family, just wandering the halls of the hospital at any hour of the day and it gave them something to focus on," she said.

Martin said she had recently noticed artwork was no longer being replaced on the walls.

"It looks clinical and a really depressing place to be - it's really quite sad."

She questioned why the hospital could not accommodate both artwork and new signage.

Royal Berkshire NHS Foundation Trust said it was "looking at different ways to improve the experience" of patients and visitors by "using the space for wayfinding solutions".

"We are exploring other areas on site that may be suitable," it added.

articles.title: Israeli attacks on Gaza kill senior education official, eight other people
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirms killing of Khaled Abu Nada, undersecretary of Education Ministry.
articles.body:
Israeli attacks have killed at least nine Palestinians across the Gaza Strip, including a senior education official and his wife, according to health officials, as attacks continued despite the ceasefire in the enclave.

Khaled Abu Nada, undersecretary of Gaza’s Ministry of Education, and his wife were killed in an air strike in western Deir el-Balah, medics at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital said on Thursday. Six other people were wounded, several of them critically.

“Without prior warning, Israeli Apache helicopters fired two missiles directly and in succession at this residential apartment,” Al Jazeera’s Ashraf Abu Amra said, reporting from Deir el-Balah. He said the area was crowded with hundreds of tents sheltering displaced families, and that the strike came during dawn prayers.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz said the attack killed Abu Nada, whom they said was “a Hamas figure responsible for the group’s economy and education portfolios”.

In northern Gaza, a drone attack on a group of people in Gaza City’s Shati refugee camp killed three people and wounded four, al-Shifa Hospital said, and a separate strike on the Tuffah neighbourhood killed three people. Another drone attack on the Nassr neighbourhood wounded several people.

Israeli gunfire also killed a 62-year-old man in eastern Bureij refugee camp, medics said.

The deaths follow a string of attacks on Gaza’s Hamas-run security services. Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, internal security chief for northern Gaza, was killed with his wife and two daughters early on Wednesday, a day after Naim Abu Nahl, Gaza’s internal security director, was killed, Al Jazeera’s Nour Khaled said, reporting from Gaza City.

“What stands out is the direct targeting by Israeli forces through the assassination of security and police commanders, ” Abu Amra said. Gaza’s Ministry of Interior has accused Israel of trying to spread chaos in the territory.

Near Israel’s so-called “Yellow Line” that marks areas under Israeli control, Israeli quadcopters drop bombs, and “some of them drop boxes loaded with explosives that blow the roofs off buildings,” Khaled said.

Gaza Health Ministry spokesperson Zaher al-Wahidi told Al Jazeera that more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed, including 130 this month, in Israeli attacks since the ceasefire took effect last October, with more than 6,000 wounded. “This is a systematic targeting of all the pillars of life in the Gaza Strip,” he said.

Gaza’s Health Ministry says 74,746 Palestinians have been killed since Israel launched its genocidal war against Palestinians in Gaza in October 2023, in response to the Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel.

articles.title: Ada Colau, candidata de Frente Amplio: "Me aparté de la política para vivir, recuperar la vida y la intimidad y reflexionar"
articles.standfirst: Así lo mencionó en la última entrevista en 'La Revuelta'
articles.summary: Así lo mencionó en la última entrevista en 'La Revuelta'
articles.body: Ada Colau ha vuelto a la política por la puerta grande. Tras haber sido alcaldesa de Barcelona durante ocho años, la política catalana, encara unos nuevos comicios como la líder de Frente Amplio pero, esta vez, en el plano nacional. Sin embargo, la política, se ha convertido en una profesión muy exigente en la que los dirigentes deben sacrificar muchos aspectos de su vida personal para cumplir con las exigencias de los puestos que ocupan. Sobre ello y el abandono inicial de la política de Colau, hablo ella misma en la entrevista de 'La Revuelta'. Sus motivos fueron puramente personales y, ella misma mencionó que se fue "para vivir, recuperar la vida y la intimidad y reflexionar". Muchas veces no somos conscientes de que necesitamos pausar nuestro trabajo (o nuestras obligaciones), aunque nuestro cuerpo nos mande señales. Sin embargo, debemos ser conscientes de que es importante parar y retomar nuestras obligaciones más adelante. Las señales de alarma suelen ser de tres tipos. Una de ellas son las físicas, entre las que se pueden encontrar el insomnio persistente, fatiga constante, dolores de cabeza, tensión muscular o malestar digestivo. Además, pueden mostrarse señales mentales y emocionales, como la dificultad para concentrarte, la niebla mental, la apatía, la irritabilidad o la desconexión. También es posible que existan señales conductuales, como tener el sentimiento de que no desconectas nunca o que el trabajo está dañando tus relaciones personales. Si necesitamos parar debemos saber cómo. En muchas ocasiones no sabemos la fórmula para hacer esa parada necesaria para mejorar nuestro bienestar físico y mental. Parar no significa que renuncies a todo de inmediato, sino que existen muchas vías para poder hacerlo. Una de ellas es consultar con un profesional sanitario, si el estrés o el agotamiento están afectando a tu salud, para que te den la baja médica. También existe la opción de tomarte un respiro solicitando días libres o vacaciones, y baraja la opción de tomarte una excedencia en caso de que sea necesario. Es importante tener una estrategia para gestionar estas situaciones más allá de la solución inmediata. Una de ellas es el cambio de rol o la implementación de límites, como reducir la carga de tareas, ajustar las expectativas o poner una barrera de disponibilidad fuera del horario. Y, si ves que te supera y puedes hacerlo, plantéate dejar el empleo. Un trabajo no debe costarte la salud aunque es importante poner en valor las necesidades económicas de cada persona.

articles.title: Hamas political official and wife among eight Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza
articles.summary: The killings are the latest from a series of near daily attacks by Israel against what it says are Hamas targets.
articles.body:
A Hamas political official and his wife were among eight Palestinians killed in three Israeli air strikes across the Gaza Strip on Thursday.

Local sources told the BBC a residential apartment in Deir al-Balah was targeted at dawn, killing Khaled Abu Nada - the deputy education minister - and his wife, Abeer Mohammed Ismail Abu Nada.

A Hamas Civil Defence spokesman said that rescue teams and medical personnel had transferred eight bodies to Al-Aqsa Hospital in central Gaza and Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza City.

In a joint statement, Israel's prime minister and defence minister said the operation was "part of a series of targeted killings" against Hamas officials.

Thursday's strikes also reportedly killed three Palestinians on al-Nafaq Street, east of Gaza City. Their identities have not yet been established, eyewitnesses said.

In a separate strike on Shati refugee camp, west of Gaza City, three Palestinians working for Hamas's security services were killed. They were identified as Yasser al-Lahham, Iyad Ahmed and Ibrahim al-Mashal.

In a post X, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the death of Khaled Abu Nada and said about 80 Hamas officials have been killed in the last month.

"No one in Hamas's leadership will succeed in evading us," he said, adding that the military would "continue to pursue our enemies and protect the security of Israeli civilians".

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it had carried out a strike on a "senior" Hamas operative, and would provide further details later.

The attacks came a day after Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, 47, the head of Hamas's internal security service in northern Gaza, his wife and their two teenage daughters were killed in Israeli air strike on their apartment in Shati refugee camp in Gaza City.

On Tuesday, the overall commander of Hamas's internal security service was among 10 Palestinians reportedly killed in Israeli strikes.

Violence has continued in Gaza since Israel and Hamas agreed to a US-brokered ceasefire in October last year. Israeli strikes take place almost daily in areas under Hamas's control, which are home to 2.1 million people, most of them displaced.

At least 1,705 people have been killed in Gaza over the past 13 months, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza during the same period.

The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Since then, more than 74,772 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, the health ministry says.

articles.title: Irene Montero, candidata de Podemos: "Para quienes consumimos carne es necesario reflexionar sobre el tipo de consumo que hacemos: es irrespetuoso con los animales, malo para nuestra salud y malo para el planeta"
articles.standfirst: La exministra y eurodiputada ha hecho mención al consumo de carne que hacemos
articles.summary: La exministra y eurodiputada ha hecho mención al consumo de carne que hacemos
articles.body: Las elecciones están dejando muchos mensajes, llamamientos y frases cargadas de potencia e ideología, como es lógico. Una de las candidatas que más fuerte está yendo en esta campaña es Irene Montero. La que fuera ministra de Igualdad y que mantiene el puesto de eurodiputada, será la líder de Podemos; haciendo campaña de la mano de Gabriel Rufián, en conjunto. Sin embargo, al margen de la postura política, Irene ha hecho referencia a otras cuestiones de interés para la ciudadanía. Una de ellas ha girado en torno a la apertura del debate de los modelos de consumo y alimentación que actualmente tiene la sociedad; tal y como reflejan desde 'El Español'. La política, quien se autodefine como consumidora de carne, menciona que merece la pena meditar sobre los hábitos cotidianos: "Para las personas que consumimos carne, es necesario reflexionar (que sé que no es suficiente) sobre que el tipo de consumo que tenemos ahora es absolutamente irrespetuoso con los animales, pero también malo para nuestra salud y malo para el planeta, insostenible". El consumo de carne en el mundo se ha disparado, en parte, por el aumento general de la población. También existe un incremento de la presencia de carne en las dietas por motivos como modas, tendencias o el auge del entrenamiento de fuerza. Y aunque debemos ser conscientes del consumo que hacemos de carne, comer carne no es malo per se. La carne es una de las mejores fuentes de proteínas completas, ya que es esencial en el mantenimiento y reparación de los tejidos, así como de la masa muscular. Pero no solo eso, también contiene micronutrientes clave como el hierro hemo, el zinc y la vitamina B12. Si bien es cierto que es un alimento con muchos beneficios, la realidad es que no debemos excedernos en su consumo. Hay muchas razones pero, una de ellas, es que entre los productos cárnicos se encuentran aquellos procesados que no son buenos ni tienen puntos positivos para los consumidores. Además, cocinarla a altas temperaturas o comerla cruda puede implicar un riesgo en para nuestra salud y bienestar. Es cierto que debemos ser conscientes de que nuestras acciones tienen consecuencias. Y el consumo de carne también la tiene y supone que un animal pierda la vida para nutrirnos. Meditar sobre ello es lo idóneo y, quienes escojan opciones veganas y vegetarianas por cuestiones tan éticas como esta, están en su derecho y deben tener opciones nutritivas, saludables y completas para cuidar su bienestar. Por otro lado, quienes son consumidores de carne deben ser conscientes de lo que supone para ellos y para los animales; intentando encontrar el equilibrio en el consumo de productos cárnicos. Los especialistas recomiendan priorizar las carnes blancas de distinto origen animal y limitar la carne roja. También es importante descartar las carnes procesadas y buscarles siempre un buen acompañamiento consistente en verduras, frutas o cereales.

articles.title: Med Emre: Diesel tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes sinks near Ibiza, killing one
articles.summary: The possible environmental damage is still being assessed by Spain's sea rescue service.
articles.body:
An oil tanker carrying up to 7,000 tonnes of diesel has sunk off the coast of Ibiza, leaving one crew member dead, authorities have said.

The Med Emre, a Malta-flagged vessel, was carrying 17 crew members who were all rescued. However seven were taken to hospital and one was later pronounced dead, Balearic Islands emergency services confirmed.

The six crew receiving treatment reportedly suffered minor injuries, such as hypothermia, Spanish media reports.

The possible environmental damage is being assessed by a plane and Spain's pollution control vessel, Clara Campoamor, which is owned by the country's national maritime rescue service.

"There is still little information available about a possible fuel spill," Balearic Islands' President Marga Prohens wrote on X.

Regional emergencies director Pablo Gárriz said the tanker had not completely sunk, and was still partially submerged.

That made conditions more favourable for carrying out recovery operations, he said, "as we have gone from the possibility of the vessel being at a depth of 1,000m to a situation that allows operations to be carried out on the surface."

The Med Emre sank 25 nautical miles (46 km; 29 miles) from Ibiza's coastline and 57 nautical miles from Valencia. It is unclear what caused the sinking.

The chemical tanker was en route from Algeciras, in southern Spain, to Barcelona in the north-east.

Rescuers in Valencia received a distress call around 22:30 local time (21:30 GMT) on Wednesday, according to Spanish media. Minutes later, the vessel reported a leak and the crew said it was leaning at a 90-degree angle.

The injured crew members have been taken to hospitals in Valencia and Can Misses Hospital in Ibiza, President Prohens said.

Ibiza's marine environment was added to the Unesco World Heritage List in 1999. In particular, it is home to dense prairies of Posidonia oceanic seagrass, which is found only in the Mediterranean basin and plays a vital role in supporting local marine biodiversity.

In 2002, Spain experienced one of its worst environmental disasters when the Prestige oil tanker ran into trouble off Galicia's coastline . It spilled more than 60,000 tonnes of heavy fuel oil into the sea.
